para.verbatim:
embed:rst Whether the ``.ini`` file carries anything to remap. ``false`` for a file that only WATCHES the character -- eg. a help overlay whose one section matches the position hash to know she is on screen, which remapped like a mod would draw a second copy of her :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` **Default**: ``true``

parameterdescription.para: Whether the file carries anything to remap

para.verbatim:
embed:rst Whether the ``.ini`` file is a RECOLOUR and nothing else: it draws none of the character's mesh, no other ``.ini`` file beside it does, and it overrides a texture of the character that the target does not draw. Its whole model then comes from downloads, with the mod's textures bound in place of the downloaded ones -- so a fixer that reads the mod's buffers while it is being built has to fetch those downloads first :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` **Default**: ``false``

parameterdescription.para: Whether the file is a recolour and nothing else

para.verbatim:
embed:rst `Sections`_ a fix writes into every ``.ini`` file it generates, so a SIBLING's toggle keeps working there: a ``[Constants]`` declaring a copy of each variable a carried recolour's condition reads, and a copy of each sibling ``[Key...]`` section that cycles one, both under the copy's name :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` A file with no ``namespace =`` is named after its PATH, so a variable of one ``.ini`` cannot be read from another. The copy is driven by the same key under the same condition, so the two keep in step :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` **Default**: empty -- nothing to carry
embed:rst Whether the mod leaves a mod object UNDRAWN -- on its own character the game never draws it, so a fix must not draw a download of it over the mod's own buffers

briefdescription.para: Records that the mod leaves 'modObj' undrawn.
Forgets every mod object addUndrawn recorded.
Every mod object the mod leaves undrawn.

para.verbatim: embed:rst The draws the mod's own `sections`_ of a mod object make with numbers, in the order they are written -- not ``drawindexed = auto``, which draws the whole of whatever is bound

embed:rst Which parts of the mod object's `sections`_ hold a ``drawindexed``, counted from 1 over every part of a `section`_ (an ``if`` line is a part too). Draws all in one part are draws under one condition
embed:rst The external libraries a mod object's `sections`_ name on any of their lines (eg. ``RabbitFX`` -- see :cpp:member:`RabbitFX::Name`), by the name the parser gives each

embed:rst The texture registers a mod object's `sections`_ bind only AFTER they have drawn, in the order first bound. A draw before them renders with whatever the game had bound, so a mod whose section draws, then binds, then draws again has two binding generations

embed:rst The texture resources a mod object's own `sections`_ bind ONLY under a toggle, lowercased: every line binding one sits in a branch that no draw of the object sits in, at a register no line reaching a draw binds. The game's own texture is what those draws render with whenever the toggle is off
embed:rst The resource a ``TextureOverride`` `section`_ with ``hash`` 'hash' puts in the texture's place with ``this =``, as written -- the first such section's -- or ``std::nullopt``

parameterdescription.para: The texture's hash, in any case

briefdescription.para: Sets thisOverrideOf, unless a resource is already recorded for 'hash'.

parameterdescription.para: The texture's hash, in any case

briefdescription.para: Whether any section_ binds 'resource' with this =.
Records that a section_ binds 'resource' with this = see isThisBound.

para.verbatim: embed:rst Whether the mod replaces a game texture BY HASH anywhere -- a texture override with a ``hash`` and a ``this =`` -- so its art reaches every draw that binds that texture, whatever the draw's own `section`_ binds

embed:rst The ``filename =`` of one of the mod's resource `sections`_, found without regard to the case of its name, or ``std::nullopt``. The value is the ``.ini``'s own (a Windows path, relative to the ``.ini``)

briefdescription.para: Every resource section_ of the mod that names a file, as lowercased name -> filename.

para.verbatim: embed:rst What role each texture of the ``.ini`` plays, or ``nullptr`` when the parser records none -- every role the ``.ini`` binds a file for, since one atlas can serve two objects

embed:rst Fills the texture data -- #textureRoles, #roleCandidates, #roleFile, #rejections -- on the first ask of any of them, rather than now :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` Sorting a mod's textures may open every one of them, and a parser is built for every ``.ini`` a run classifies, most of which no fixer asks about

parameterdescription.para: What fills them, or empty for nothing

para.verbatim: embed:rst The file a mod object takes for a role, or ``nullptr`` when no file of the mod serves the role -- the choice among #roleCandidates is per mod object, since a file a mod binds on one object is the better answer for that object
embed:rst The ``this =`` toggle that chooses a resource, or ``nullptr`` -- a texture override ``hash = <a texture> / if ... this = A / else this = B`` the mod writes to swap one texture for another

briefdescription.para: Records the this = toggle that chooses 'resource'.

para.verbatim: embed:rst The register toggle that chooses a resource, or ``nullptr`` -- one `section`_ binding one register to several resources on its branches (``if $x == 1 / ps-t3 = A / else / ps-t3 = B``)

briefdescription.para: Records the register toggle that chooses 'resource'.
Every file refused for a role, in the order they were refused.

para.verbatim: embed:rst The game version whose skeleton numbering the mod's blend gives its bone ids in, when the parser could tell from the mod's geometry -- a mod's hashes may name one version while its bone ids are another's. ``std::nullopt`` when the parser did not ask or could not tell

briefdescription.para: Records that the .ini's resource section_ 'resource' names the texture 'file'.

parameterdescription.para: The file, as roleFile and rejections name it

para.verbatim: embed:rst What a texture line binding 'resource' binds: every ``(role, mod object)`` the parser chose the resource's file for (#roleFile) -- or a file of the same toggle (:cpp:member:`RoleFile::variants`) -- by role and then by mod object. Empty for a resource naming no texture, or one chosen for nothing

parameterdescription.para: The resource section_, in any case

briefdescription.para: The role the parser REFUSED the resource's file for (the first of rejections), or std::nullopt.

parameterdescription.para: The resource section_, in any case
Why, as a sentence about the file

para.verbatim:
embed:rst The rows of the :cpp:class:`GraphCollect` named 'name' among the parser's :cpp:member:`GIMIParser::parseSteps`, in the order it collected them. Empty for a name nothing filed
.. warning:: The rows describe the graphs as they were when the collect ran (see :cpp:class:`GraphCollect`). A collect among :cpp:member:`GIMIParser::deferredParseSteps` runs on the FIRST ask of this data, so that first ask has to come before any edit to the graphs it reads: a fixer asks in its constructor, before its edits run. Asked first after an edit, the rows are read from the edited graphs

memberdef.argsstring: (const std::string &name, const std::string &section, const std::string &key) const
memberdef.name: firstCollected

para.verbatim: embed:rst The first row of the :cpp:class:`GraphCollect` named 'name' that holds 'key' in 'section' itself -- not in a section it ``run =``\s -- in the order the collect found them. 'section' is matched regardless of case, as 3DMigoto matches a section's name; 'key' exactly. ``nullptr`` when there is none

briefdescription.para: Files 'rows' under 'name', replacing what was filed there see collected.

para.verbatim: embed:rst Reads the mod's anatomy off collected rows and records it: each resource's file (#resourceFiles), and for each object its numbered draws (#drawRanges) and the parts they sit in (#drawParts), the texture registers it binds only after it has drawn (#lateBindings, unless #replacesTexturesByHash), the libraries it names (#libraries), the texture resources it binds only under a toggle (#toggledBindings), and whether it is hidden -- its `sections`_ draw nothing and skip the game's draw (#isUndrawn). Given :cpp:member:`AnatomyRules::sections`, also every ``this =`` override (#thisOverrideOf, #isThisBound). Only the rows in an object's own root `sections`_ count, except that a draw or a ``run =`` anywhere it reaches counts as drawing

embed:rst What a parser learned about a ``.ini`` file that a fixer needs and cannot read off the sections it is handed -- the classification data a parser keeps, whatever the game :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` Every :cpp:class:`BaseIniParser` owns one (:cpp:func:`BaseIniParser::parseData`): the parser fills it while it parses, and a fixer reads it through the parser it is given. A parser that fills nothing leaves the defaults, which say "everything is there": the file has something to remap, no mod object is undrawn, and no texture has a known role :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` A mod object is ``(component, object)``, as the parser's graphs are keyed -- eg. ``("Body", "C")`` for a slot of a GI component, ``("", "component3")`` for a Wuthering Waves draw slot :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` What the mod's textures ARE comes in three layers, each read off the one before: which roles each file plays (#textureRoles), the candidates left for each role once the files that cannot serve it are refused (#roleCandidates, #rejections), and the one file each mod object takes for a role (#roleFile). The expensive ones may be filled on the first ask -- see #defer
